newsitem.title: USA: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD - Stocks to eye earnings, data.
newsitem.headline: WALL ST WEEK AHEAD - Stocks to eye earnings, data.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, struggling for their footing after a sharp pullback, will turn this week to a key piece of economic data and fourth-quarter earnings reports from companies including Coca-Cola Co and Procter & Gamble Co.
Market watchers said that the downdraft in stocks that began with a 94-point Dow loss on Thursday is likely to carry through this week as investors take further profits from the New Year's rally.
"This market has been in a danger zone for the last five or six sessions," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments.
While saying the market's underlying fundamentals remain strong, Cardillo added, "I can see it going down a total of five percent."
The Dow industrials ened the week off 137 points, or two percent, at 6696.
The blue chip index had risen over seven percent in January through Thursday's intra-session high, before reversing its course.
A report on the fourth quarter Employee Cost Index, a barometer of how much companies pay for employees, will be closely watched by both equities and bond markets.
Analysts said a higher-than-expected ECI number could damage the inflation-sensitive bond market and rekindle fears of a Federal Reserve hike in interest rates.
"People are looking at that for (signs of) inflation pressure on wages," said Bruce Bittles, market strategist at J.C. Bradford.

Economists generally expect the ECI to rise 0.9 percent in the fourth quarter, compared with a 0.6 percent gain in the third quarter. The report is due ahead of the stock market's opening Tuesday at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.
Analysts said they will also be paying close attention to fourth-quarter profit reports from large consumer products companies such as Coke and Procter & Gamble.
Beyond the earnings per share numbers, market players said they will also look for any indication from the companies that the recent strength in the dollar will hurt future profits.
While large-capitalization stocks could be hurt by the effects of the strong dollar, small-cap shares, which have lagged the big caps so far this year, may benefit, Bittles said.
Multinationals see their foreign earnings shaved by a strong dollar, while smaller companies can benefit by paying less in dollar terms for imported raw materials.
Companies expected to report earnings this week, accompanied by their First Call estimates versus year-ago figures, include:
* Coca-Cola Q4 $0.31 vs $0.26
* Eli Lilly and Co Q4 $0.68 vs $0.57
* Merck and Co Inc Q4 $0.86 vs $0.70
* Procter & Gamble Q2 $1.32 vs $1.18
* Atlantic Richfield Co Q4 $2.49 vs $2.13
* Netscape Communications Corp Q4 $0.10 vs $0.03
* Amdahl Corp Q4 profit $0.13 vs loss $0.32
* Tambrands Inc Q4 $0.64 vs $0.63
